need.statement: Let our coding agent open our web application in a real browser, click through a flow, fill in forms, and take screenshots, so that it can test UI changes.
need.relevant: The capability lets an agent drive a real browser interactively (navigate, click, type, read the page or take screenshots).
need.partial: Browser automation that an agent cannot use directly (a plain library), or page fetching or scraping without interaction.

need.statement: Let an agent read and update GitHub issues and pull requests in our repositories: read them, comment, label, and open pull requests.
need.relevant: The capability gives an agent read and write operations on GitHub issues and pull requests.
need.partial: GitHub-related but narrower (one workflow only, such as fixing CI or answering review comments) or read-only.

need.statement: Give an agent live web search, with result URLs it can cite, for questions about current information.
need.relevant: The capability runs web search queries and returns results with their URLs.
need.partial: Fetches or scrapes a given URL without searching, or searches a single site or a closed corpus.

need.statement: Extract the text and tables from PDF files inside an agent workflow.
need.relevant: The capability reads existing PDF files and returns their text, and tables where present.
need.partial: Converts PDFs or other documents to text or Markdown without table handling, or handles PDFs only as one format among many without stating extraction.

truthGroups.basis: The registry entry declares npm @playwright/mcp and the package's mcpName points back to it; the Docker entry is built from microsoft/playwright-mcp; the plugin (plugin.json and .mcp.json only) runs npx @playwright/mcp@latest.

The registry entry declares the image ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server and the hosted endpoint https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/; the Docker entry uses that image and repository; the plugin (.mcp.json only) connects to the same endpoint.
The registry entry declares the npm package; its mcpName points back.
The registry entry declares the PyPI package, and the package description carries the mcp-name marker.
